extracted.intended_audience: Members of Parliament, East India Company officials, policymakers, and historians reading the Select Committee report
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and committee correspondence evaluating East India Company administration of Carnatic/Tanjore revenues, management, and leases; offers practical standards for revenue administration, treatment of renters, and safeguards against abuse. Intended as a formal inquiry-report addressing governance and fiscal management in a specific colonial context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy and retrenchment of expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation of a considerable and immediate reduction of expenses across districts; when in doubt prefer retrenching too much rather than too little.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee chose to 'incur the hazard of retrenching too much than too little' because 'it would be easier, after any stated allowance for expenses, to add what might be necessary than to diminish.' They expect no material increase later and stress rigid economy as necessary to recover provinces from mismanagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement of corrupt or obstructive aumildars/administrators
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocated a total change of the principal aumildars employed under the Nabob and appointment of renters under the Company's sole authority where local servants obstructed recovery of revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Nabob's servants evaded orders and refused accounts; the committee judged success only possible by appointing renters under Company authority and publicly advertising to attract bidders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent and accurate accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Require full accounts of management and collection; obtain materials leading to perfect knowledge of former and present state of districts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee complaints that 'no attention was paid to the strong and repeated applications made to them for the accounts' and that orders were evaded. Emphasis on compiling reliable records before altering management or making further commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public advertisement and fair lease procedures to encourage bidders
rubrics_metrics.description: Let districts by public advertisement in the Company's name, circulated through every province, advertising for the whole period of the Nabob's assignment and promising the Company's protection to renters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This method successfully produced numerous proposals and favorable terms; attempts to counteract the plan were taken as proof of its necessity. Guidance includes broad circulation and clear promise of protection to encourage responsible bidders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate military from civil/administrative charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Discriminate charges incurred for troops (defence) from those for sibbendy, servants, cultivation and collection of revenues, and from customary public charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee noted previous blending of disparate charges under a confused title which allowed fraud and appropriation. Proper classification is necessary to identify genuine district expenses and to prevent concealment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for customary rights and public charities while trimming excessive ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay attention to established customs, ancient privileges of inhabitants, and public charities that are 'necessarily allowed and appeared proper to be continued', but prevent their being rated excessively or used to conceal misappropriation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow customary items where appropriate, but avoid inflated or blended ratings that served as pretexts for fraud and oppression under the Nabob's government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection and legal security for renters/leaseholders (third parties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before surrendering assignments, consider how it will affect third persons who entered into covenants/leases with the Company; leases (3–5 years per assignment) cannot be legally torn from renters except for their prior breach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee treats safeguarding renters as 'an act of strict and necessary justice'—the Company (and public faith) is bound to maintain leases during their term; abrupt removal would amount to arbitrary despotism and expose renters to vengeance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid blending expense categories to conceal fraud or appropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticize the practice of blending various district expenses under one confused and unintelligible title, which afforded latitude for every species of fraud and oppression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report links blended expense categories to secret appropriation of revenues and calls for itemized, intelligible accounts to prevent concealment and mismanagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlistment or discharge of Nabob's sepoys to reduce fiscal burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Receive into the Company's service such of the Nabob's sibbendies, sepoys, and horsemen as will enlist, and discharge the rest, thereby relieving country of heavy burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All charges under that head were struck out of the committee's expense account; if enlistment is partial or subsequent military additions are needed, their cost must be deducted from present savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer managers acquainted with local customs and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid letting districts to outsiders ignorant of local manners/customs; such management oppressed inhabitants, caused desertion of cultivation, and led to failure of collections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence showed leases to strangers led to oppression and decline of cultivation; recommendation to entrust districts to persons of the country or otherwise ensure local-knowledge management to secure revenue and stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderate revenue demands in accordance with capacity; require financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Government should adapt demands to the Rajah's circumstances and not impose sums beyond ability to pay; should request statements of accounts, disbursements, debts, and payments to ascertain real capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Witness testimony that Rajah of Tanjore was not able to meet onerous deposits or jaghires, sometimes borrowing at exorbitant rates; committee criticizes attempts to exact payments without assessing the country's finances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and fund essential public infrastructure (Anicut/irrigation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize large irrigation works (the Anicut) as essential to prosperity and require their regular repair and funding; neglect leads to overflow, parching, and general injury to the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee records that neglect or attempts to damage the Anicut (possibly instigated by neighboring powers) threaten all other works and agriculture; preserving such works is a priority for sustained revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against concentration of power in untrustworthy intermediaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not entrust or employ persons who have shown tendencies to pursue projects injurious to Company or individuals (example: Mr. Benfield, Amir-ul-Omrah); restraint on their power is recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee reports that such persons had 'prosecuted projects to the injury and danger of the Company' and that their continuance in positions of influence would be 'improper to trust, and dangerous to employ'—advocates removal or restraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure accurate, intelligible language and faithful translations in official correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid practices that render the Nabob or other principals unable to understand the true contents of communications (for example, substituting translations that enable intermediaries to misrepresent or manipulate meaning).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee criticizes transmitting documents in English via interpreters rather than preserving Persian originals; warns that double channels and unfaithful translation allow others to 'inspire' and substitute sentiments and signatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uphold public faith—honour mutual covenants and obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that mutual and strict covenants between the Company and renters create reciprocal obligations; the Company and its constituents are bound by public faith to maintain agreed terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee emphasizes the sacred obligation to truth and justice in reporting and administering leases—breach of covenants would amount to an assumption of sovereignty and arbitrary despotism, and thus must be avoided.
